summary: This is the first lecture in a series on the life of the Prophet Muhammad SAW for children, and it begins before he was born. The ustaz explains how poor Mecca became rich through the trade started by Hashim, the Prophet's great-grandfather. He then tells of Abraha, the king of Yemen, who built the church of Kulais and came with an army of elephants to destroy the Kaaba. Abdul Muttalib said the Kaaba has a Lord who protects it, and Allah SWT sent flocks of ababil birds that destroyed the army. That is why the Prophet SAW is said to have been born in the Year of the Elephant.
keyPoints: Mecca used to be poor and the zamzam water was lost, until Hashim, the Prophet's great-grandfather, began trading between Syam and Yemen.
Abraha built the church of Kulais to draw people away from the Kaaba, and when it was defiled he vowed to destroy the Kaaba.
The elephant army came to Mecca and Abdul Muttalib only asked for his camels back, because the Kaaba has a Lord who protects it.
The elephant named Mahmud refused to move towards the Kaaba, and ababil birds dropped hot stones on Abraha's army.
This happened while the Prophet SAW was still in Aminah's womb, so it is called the Year of the Elephant.
The story is recorded in Surah Al-Fil.

chapters.title: The start of the series on the Prophet's life
chapters.summary: The first lecture begins before the Prophet SAW was born, with the story behind Surah Al-Fil and the Year of the Elephant.

chapters.title: A poor Mecca
chapters.summary: Mecca used to be poor, with little water or food because the zamzam water had been lost.

chapters.title: Hashim and the trade route
chapters.summary: Hashim saw goods from China, India and Africa reaching Syam and Yemen, and thought about how to bring them to Mecca.

chapters.title: Hashim's two yearly journeys
chapters.summary: Hashim went to Syam when Mecca was hot and to Yemen when Mecca was cool, bringing goods back to Mecca.

chapters.title: Mecca grows rich, and the idols at the Kaaba
chapters.summary: Mecca grew rich, and idols were kept at the Kaaba so that robbers would not trouble the Quraysh caravans.

chapters.title: Abraha builds the church of Kulais
chapters.summary: Abraha, the new king of Yemen from Africa, built a great church called Kulais to rival the Kaaba.

chapters.title: Kulais is defiled and Abraha vows revenge
chapters.summary: A man from Mecca relieved himself inside Kulais, so Abraha grew angry and vowed to destroy the Kaaba with elephants.

chapters.title: The elephant army heads for Mecca
chapters.summary: Elephants, which the Arabs had never seen, were likened to tanks that flattened houses along the way.

chapters.title: The guide from Taif
chapters.summary: An Arab from Taif showed the way, and Abraha's army camped near Mecca and seized camels.

chapters.title: Abdul Muttalib meets Abraha
chapters.summary: Abraha stood up in awe, but Abdul Muttalib only asked for his camels and said the Kaaba has its Owner.

chapters.title: Mecca is emptied and Abdul Muttalib prays
chapters.summary: The people went up to the hillsides, Abdul Muttalib prayed at the door of the Kaaba, and Aminah was there carrying the Prophet SAW in her womb.

chapters.title: The elephant Mahmud refuses to move
chapters.summary: The elephant named Mahmud would not head for the Kaaba even when beaten and prodded.

chapters.title: The ababil birds and the army's destruction
chapters.summary: A dark cloud of ababil birds came carrying hot stones, and Abraha's army was destroyed.

chapters.title: The Year of the Elephant and Surah Al-Fil
chapters.summary: A flood cleansed Mecca, the event was called the Year of the Elephant, and its story is recorded in Surah Al-Fil.

books.context: The ustaz mentions that this sirah book writes the elephant's name as Mahmud.
A summary of the sirah covering conditions in Arabia before the Prophet's birth and the Year of the Elephant.

people.context: A very clever man. He began the trade between Syam and Yemen that made Mecca rich.
He came from Africa, built Kulais, then brought an army of elephants to destroy the Kaaba.
An Arab from Taif who helped Abraha's army because his idols were not at the Kaaba. His grave was made a place to relieve oneself, as a sign of disgrace for a traitor.
Aminah's husband, who had already passed away when the elephant army came.
She was a few months pregnant with the Prophet SAW at the time and went up to the hillside with the people of Mecca.

people.role: Grandfather of the Prophet SAW and leader of the Quraysh
people.context: He asked Abraha for his camels and said the Kaaba has a Lord who protects it, then prayed at the door of the Kaaba.

people.role: Wife of the Prophet SAW, Mother of the Believers
people.context: She related that she still saw the blind beggars in Mecca who had once helped Abraha's army.

lessons.title: Allah protects His House
lessons.body: Abdul Muttalib said the Kaaba has a Lord who will protect it. Allah SWT truly protected it from a mighty army.

lessons.title: Pray and rely on Allah
lessons.body: After emptying Mecca, Abdul Muttalib held the door of the Kaaba and prayed that Allah would save it.

lessons.title: Military might cannot overcome Allah's will
lessons.body: A very strong army and its elephants were destroyed by small birds at the command of Allah SWT.

lessons.title: Creatures obey Allah's command
lessons.body: The elephant Mahmud refused to head for the Kaaba because Allah had told it not to attack.

lessons.title: Anger and revenge lead to ruin
lessons.body: Abraha grew furious and vowed to destroy the Kaaba, and in the end he perished with his army.

lessons.title: Effort and thinking change a people's fortune
lessons.body: Hashim thought ahead and opened a trade route, and poor Mecca became rich.

lessons.title: Betrayal brings disgrace
lessons.body: The guide from Taif who helped Abraha's army died, and his grave was made a place to relieve oneself as a sign of disgrace.

lessons.title: A leader's presence and calm
lessons.body: Abdul Muttalib had such presence that Abraha stood up in awe, yet he stayed calm and clear in his stand.

lessons.title: The Prophet SAW was protected even in the womb
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW was still in Aminah's womb, only a few months along, when Allah saved the Kaaba.

lessons.title: Surah Al-Fil records this story
lessons.body: The surah we often recite turns out to tell of the elephant army, which came before the Prophet SAW was born.

glossary.meaning: The year of the elephant army's attack, which marks the year of the Prophet's birth because the Arabs then had no numbered calendar.
The water that had been lost at that time and that the people of Mecca could not find.
The cool northern region where Hashim collected leather goods and silk.
The Arab tribe of Mecca, who traded to Syam and Yemen.
The great church Abraha built in Yemen to rival the Kaaba.
The birds Allah sent carrying hot stones to destroy Abraha's army.
The hot, sharp stones thrown by the ababil birds.

dalil.context: The ustaz recites Surah Al-Fil as the source of the story of the elephant army.
dalil.translation: Do you [Prophet] not see how your Lord dealt with the army of the elephant?

dalil.context: Allah made their plan come to nothing.
dalil.translation: Did He not utterly confound their plans?

dalil.context: Allah sent ababil birds upon them.
dalil.translation: He sent ranks of birds against them,

dalil.context: The birds threw hot, sharp sijjil stones.
dalil.translation: pelting them with pellets of hard-baked clay:

dalil.context: As a result they became like leaves eaten away.

sirah.era: Before the Prophet's birth: the Year of the Elephant
sirah.summary: This lecture tells of the elephant army's attack on the Kaaba while the Prophet SAW was still in his mother's womb, which is why the year of his birth is called the Year of the Elephant.
